This application, under section 482 of Cr.P.C. has been filed for quashment of FIR in Crime No.951/2022 registered at Police Station Civil Line, District Morena for offences under sections 498A, 294, 506, 34 of IPC.
2.

sentences.text: Prosecution story, in short, is that respondent No. 6 lodged an FIR on 12.10.2022 stating that she is residing in her matrimonial house situated in Prem Nagar, Jaura, District Morena.
She lost her husband in the month of February 2022 and has three children namely Aditi Sharma, aged about 11 years, Vedant Sharma, aged about 6 years, and Vivansh aged about 2 years.
It is alleged that applicants are intending to oust her from her matrimonial house.
They abuse her filthily in the name of mother and sister and also extend threats to her life.

Since they are intending to oust her,
therefore, they abuse her and threaten that she should leave the house.
Accordingly, the FIR in question was lodged.
4. By referring to allegations of respondent No. 6, it is submitted by counsel for applicants that respondent No. 6 has lodged the FIR on flimsy grounds.
It is submitted that in the Police statement of respondent No. 6 recorded on 12.10.2022, she has specifically stated that her husband was in Army and attained martyrdom about 10 months back.
She does not have any brother and has two more sisters.

Her father, Satish, had expired many years ago, and she is residing with her mother,
Girja.
She has three children namely Aditi Sharma, Vedant Sharma, and Vivaansh.
At present, she is residing in Government Murar Thapa Quarter, Gwalior.

After her husband attained martyrdom,
whatever amount was received by her is the only source of her livelihood.
Her parental home is in Nayapura, Ambah, and one parental house is also situated in Pratap Colony, Ambah.
It was alleged that applicants are intending to oust her from her matrimonial house.
Accordingly, they abuse her in the name of mother and sister, and whenever she refuses to leave the house, they extend threats to her life.
They want to dispossess her from the house in which her husband had a share.

Since she is not vacating the house, applicants are harassing her physically and mentally, and for that reason,
she is residing in the Government quarter in Gwalior.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:8292 3 MISC. CRIMINAL CASE No. 56271 of 2022

It is submitted that in fact, respondent No. 6 never resided with the applicants, and she has been residing in the Government quarter and with an intention to claim partition during the lifetime of applicant Nos. 1 and 2, she has lodged a false FIR.
5. Per contra, the application is vehemently opposed by counsel for the State as well as respondent No. 6.

Counsel for State, after going through the statement of respondent No. 6 recorded under Section 161 of Cr.P.C, has fairly conceded that in her statement, respondent No. 6 has admitted twice that she is residing in her Government quarter at Morar, District Gwalior.

Accordingly, counsel for the complainant was directed to explain that when the Government quarter was allotted to respondent No. 6 or her husband, and since when she is residing in the said Government quarter?
Counsel for Respondent No. 6 was not in a position to answer the aforesaid query raised by the Court.

6. Heard learned counsel for the parties.

sentences.text:
As already mentioned above, in her statement recorded under Section 161 of Cr.P.C, respondent No. 6 has specifically clarified that she is residing in a Government quarter situated at Morar,
District Gwalior.

Case diary also contains one application made by respondent No. 6 to the SHO of Police Station Civil Lines, District Morena, in which she has specifically stated that her in-laws are not ready to give her share in the ancestral property and requested serious action against them.

entities.text: Police Station Civil Lines, District Morena
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Thus, it is clear that respondent No. 6 is interested in a share in the ancestral property.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:8292 4 MISC. CRIMINAL CASE No. 56271 of 2022 8.

Now, the only question for consideration is as to whether respondent No. 6 was ousted by the applicants after the death of her husband, or whether she was already residing separately in the Government quarter in Gwalior, and the allegation of being ousted from the matrimonial house situated in Morena is false?
9.

As already pointed out, this Court had requested counsel for respondent No. 6 to point out the date when the Government quarter situated in Morar, Gwalior was allotted to her husband, or, if it was allotted after his death, then the date of such allotment to respondent No.6.
Counsel for Respondent No. 6 could not give any answer to this query.

Since her husband was in the Army, and a large portion of Morar, District Gwalior, is Army area, and respondent No. 6 is residing in a Government quarter, it is clear that the said quarter must have been allotted to her husband while he was in service.
Therefore, respondent No. 6 must have been residing in the Government quarter in Gwalior from the date of its allotment.
If Respondent No. 6 was already in occupation of government accommodation in Gwalior, then the allegation that applicants are trying to oust her from ancestral property situated in Morena is false.
As already pointed out, the real intention behind filing the application is to claim a share in the ancestral property.
10. It is a well-established principle of law that any effort made by a party to convert a civil litigation into criminal litigation must be foiled.
If respondent No. 6 is of the view that she has a share in the ancestral property, then she has to file a suit for partition.
(This Court has not given any finding as to whether the property in question is ancestral or self-acquired property of applicant No. 1.)
It is not the case of respondent No. 6 that she was treated with cruelty for any other reason.

11. Under the circumstances, this Court is of considered opinion that the FIR lodged by Respondent No. 6 does not disclose commission of offence under NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:8292 5 MISC. CRIMINAL CASE No. 56271 of 2022 Section 498A of IPC, but it appears that it is an attempt to seek partition of property.
